Subject: Re: Intro + POC goals (recap & next steps)

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we kick off the POC: 

Summary of what you want to validate:
- Latency at <150ms p95 for single-user interactive flows (up to 1024 tokens)
- Sustained throughput for batch reranking at ~60 qps during evaluation windows
- Quality parity vs your in-house baseline on the privacy-sensitive dataset (10k eval prompts)

Success criteria (suggested):
1) p95 latency <= 150ms for 1-2 concurrent interactive sessions using our recommended config
2) Batch throughput >= 50 qps for the reranking job with <=3% error rate
3) No data exfiltration issues; logs limited to request IDs and telemetry as scoped in the DPA

Capacity discussion (initial recommendation):
- Start with 2 reserved GPUs (NVIDIA A100 40GB equiv) for the baseline workload.
- Autoscaling policy to add up to 4 additional GPU workers for burst windows (up to 6 total) — burst scale target for nightly eval runs.
- If you expect sustained >200 qps we should move to 4 reserved GPUs from day 1.

Next steps / owners: 
- ZenStack: confirm expected peak qps for both interactive and batch eval jobs + provide sample eval dataset (Priya) — due Wed, Mar 18
- Redwood: produce POC MAP and pricing estimate + detailed autoscale config (Marissa / Rishi) — deliver Thu, Mar 18
- Schedule tech deep-dive to lock pipelining/batching details (Rishi to lead) — propose 1 hour slot next week

Attachments: POC MAP draft and scope worksheet (see attached).

If that looks right I’ll create the HubSpot MOP and send calendar invites for the deep-dive.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks for the context — quick technical notes on capacity and autoscaling so everyone has the same expectations: 

Baseline recommended config for POC:
- Reserved: 2x A100-40GB equiv workers (pinned for predictable latency).
- Burst: autoscale pool up to +4 additional workers (max 6 total).
- Instance warm-up: ~45-90s for new workers to be ready (image pull + runtime init) — we recommend a small pre-warm window 5-10 minutes before scheduled nightly evals to avoid initial latency spikes.
- Batching: we’ll enable continuous batching with a 40ms max latency cap for interactive traffic which should keep p95 under 150ms for 1-2 user sessions; for larger concurrency we’ll shift to dynamic batching thresholds.
- KV cache: recommend enabling prefix cache for reranking use-case to cut repeat-token compute.

Cost-ish notes (high level):
- Reserved GPUs priced in attached quote; burst workers billed at on-demand rates for the POC period. I’ll include numbers in the POC MAP.

Next steps from engineering side:
- Dev to share a short runbook for pre-warm scripting and the eval job orchestration (Dev) — ETA Wed, Mar 18 EOD.
- Rishi to send the autoscale JSON snippet we use to plug into your scheduler (coming tomorrow).

— Rishi
